label: t/c/y/g/q input at original positions 3-5 after an m/h/z/l/v/e/w prefix
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase, almost entirely at positions t=3-5 (95% of mass; a little at t=2 and t=6, never at t<2 or t>=7, never on the delimiter or copy phase). The input token sets it: t (39% of mass, about 10x lift), then c, y, g, q; a and o give weak activations. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of that token. The earlier prefix modulates it: it is stronger and more likely when the earlier inputs include m/h/z/l/v/e/w (top examples look like m h z v [t]) and weaker when the prefix has digits or already contains t/c/y/g/q. The strongest activations are t at t=3-4 after such a prefix. The predicate gets mass recall about 0.83 on dev but precision only about 0.35: many t/c/y/g/q inputs at t=3-5 do not cross the threshold, so the dependence on the prefix seems graded rather than a clean rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=m (+2.81), orig0=h (+2.64), orig0=z (+2.61), phase=0 & in_tok=c (+2.48), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=c (+2.48), orig0=l (+2.44). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.09), t=8 (-5.55), t=7 (-5.11), prev2_tok=- (-4.21).
